Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot. Sorry for the confusion.

Short explanation: sometimes Google Calendar shows a "floating" time when an event creator's calendar timezone doesn't match the event TZID or when an invite is forwarded between accounts with different default timezone settings. We also see issues during daylight saving transitions if an event doesn't include explicit timezone info. Looks like our initial invite was created from a calendar set to PST and then forwarded; that can cause recipients to see it shifted.

Workarounds I recommend:
- I'll recreate the event explicitly set to UTC (TZ=UTC) and include the time in the title (e.g., "Redwood demo — 15:00 UTC / 11:00 ET / 16:00 BST").
- I'll attach a properly generated .ics that includes TZID entries and send it from my calendar (not forwarded).
- If anyone still sees the wrong time, please open the event in Google Calendar and check Settings -> Time zone for the event and your calendar default time zone.

I'll send a fresh invite for Wed Apr 21 at 15:00 UTC (three time columns in the description) and include the Zoom link. If that doesn't work, we can provide three discrete options (see below) and let you pick.

-Jonas
